title: Controlled fault-injection evaluation of verifier-guided LLM repair on vendor CLIs (paired design)
research_question: Does a deterministic verifier-guided LLM repair pipeline reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared to blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults across Cisco and Juniper task templates?
confirmatory_hypotheses: Verifier-guided repair will yield a higher proportion of configurations that pass the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and simulator-based compliance check than blind repair on the same injected faults (guarded > baseline).

With n = 40 paired tasks the paired difference in verifier pass rates is estimable; a two-sided exact paired test will detect an absolute guarded-minus-baseline difference of approximately 30 percentage points or larger under the preregistered assumptions.
Verifier-guided repair will not increase harmful over-repair events beyond the prespecified safety threshold (<= 5% absolute increase).
exploratory_questions: How do pass-rate improvements vary by fault class (e.g., missing BGP neighbor vs. ACL order inversion)?
What proportion of repairs produce substantive intent-changing edits flagged by the frozen harmful-change rules (exploratory descriptive only)?
benchmark_scope: Controlled fault-injection vendor-CLI task bank (Cisco + Juniper) constructed from public configuration templates
Task bank limited to the 40 preregistered controlled-fault indices (1..40) generated by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1
model_scope: Hosted model API (provider: openai_responses). Exact model_name and model_version will be selected at execution and recorded in the execution manifest; model identifier(s) will be archived and hashed.
sampling_plan: Preregistered controlled-challenge, paired, shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Confirmatory task_count = 40 (exact). Task indices: consecutive integers 1..40 (adapter-mandated). For each of the 40 tasks: generate one shared faulty candidate (source_generation_calls_per_task=1), execute exactly two repair episodes (baseline + guarded). Episodes_per_task=2. Arithmetic: 40 tasks * up to 3 model calls per task = 120 model calls total as specified by the adapter (one source generation call + up to two repair calls where eligible). Total confirmatory repair attempts = 40 tasks * 2 conditions = 80 repair attempts. Selection and fault assignment are deterministic and outcome-independent (fault_assignment_seed=17). All generation, fault operators, and task-generation code are archived and hashed before execution.
analysis_plan: Use available analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' to compute the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Primary test: exact paired binary test (McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial test) on verifier+simulator pass/fail per condition. Report absolute risk difference with 95% CI, exact paired discordant counts, and two-sided p-value. Secondary analyses: per-fault-class descriptive risk differences with CIs (exploratory). Cost analysis: report model-call counts, elapsed wall-clock per episode, and compute model_call_cost_per_avoided_failure with bootstrap CIs. All model-call / latency instrumentation and seeds recorded. The analysis executor's failed_call_treatment options will be applied as preregistered: primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude task if both condition executions fail infrastructure-wise); sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat technical failure as a failed repair outcome) and reported alongside the primary result.
multiplicity_plan: Single predefined primary paired test (no multiplicity adjustment). Secondary subgroup and descriptive results labeled exploratory and reported with CIs; no confirmatory claims from exploratory analyses.
missingness_plan: Technical-execution failures are logged as infrastructure failures. Primary analysis applies the adapter/analysis default 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with incomplete executions) and reports the number and cause of exclusions. Sensitivity analysis treats missing repair outputs as failures (worst-case) per the analysis executor option and is reported alongside the primary result.

benchmark_names: Controlled vendor-CLI task bank (preregistered; public templates)
risk_factors: Overlap between public templates used in task bank and any model training data (hosted model nondeterminism / public-corpus contamination)
detection_procedures: Deterministic string-match scanning of generated tasks and faults against archived task bank to prevent task leakage during generation.
Record and compare verifier labels to simulator outcomes for a disjoint verifier↔simulator concordance validation set (disjoint from confirmatory 1..40) before confirmatory execution.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any task where the verifier reports pass but simulator reports fail (verifier/simulator disagreement) for analytic categorization; disagreements will be analyzed but not excluded from confirmatory counts.
Flag any repair that removes or disables configured objects listed in the frozen 'protected-intent' schema (e.g., pre-declared ACL entries or interface shutdowns) for automatic harmful-change counts.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Disagreements are reported descriptively and included in the primary paired pass/fail outcome only when simulator-based ground-truth and verifier agree on pass; primary estimator uses deterministic vendor-CLI verifier pass AND simulator-based compliance pass as the combined success flag. Sensitivity analyses present results using verifier-only success and simulator-only success.
residual_uncertainty: Potential model training-data overlap with public templates (residual uncertainty despite detection procedures).
Limited ability of simulator to capture all production dynamics; residual external-validity uncertainty.

budget_scenarios.description: Execute adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with confirmatory task_count = 40. Use hosted model API (openai_responses); exact model_name/model_version selected at execution and recorded. Use the frozen controlled_fault_source and transformations. Single-repair budget per condition (baseline blind; guarded validator diagnostics + one repair).
models: openai_responses (model_name and model_version to be recorded at execution)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Adapter requires multiples of 40 and estimates exactly task_count*3 model calls; with task_count=40 this equals 120 model calls which matches the capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (120). All required operations are supported by the hosted-model API and deterministic adapter contract; no human annotation or external partners required.

budget_scenarios.description: Same confirmatory design (adapter v2, 40 tasks) executed with a lower-cost hosted model variant if available (to be selected before execution). Identical task bank and transformations; preserves the same deterministic counts and adapter contract.
models: openai_responses (lower-cost model variant if available; model identifier recorded)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Matches adapter and manifest constraints (40 tasks, 120 model calls). Provides a lower-cost execution option while keeping all scientific design elements identical; model id recorded for traceability.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute paired success-rate difference of ~30 percentage points (guarded minus baseline)
power_plan.clustering_unit: task (paired: same faulty candidate, two repair conditions)
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired-binary detectable effect reasoning for McNemar/exact paired test with n=40. With n=40 pairs, alpha=0.05 two-sided, and an expected nontrivial discordant-pair proportion, the design reliably detects absolute paired differences on the order of ~0.30 (30 percentage points) or larger with ≈80% power under cooperative discordant distributions. Smaller effects have reduced power; sensitivity analyses report exact detectable effect sizes given observed discordant counts.
assumptions: Primary success flag requires verifier AND simulator agreement on pass; baseline paired pass rate assumed between 0.25–0.50 for planning purposes.
Discordant pairs proportion (tasks where conditions disagree) is non-negligible (>0.25) for power to approach 80%.
Two-sided alpha = 0.05, primary test = exact paired binary test (McNemar/exact).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: Under conservative assumptions (discordant rate ~0.30), n=40 gives ~80% power to detect ≈30 percentage-point absolute paired differences. If observed discordant counts are lower, detectable effect size increases; report exact post hoc detectable-effect curves and conduct sensitivity analyses for smaller effect sizes.
sensitivity_analyses: Primary analysis reported together with sensitivity treating technical failures as failures (failed_call_treatment option).
Report detectable-effect curves conditional on observed discordant pair counts (tabulated).

semantic_equivalence_checks: Automatic diff-based semantic check: if repair modifies only whitespace/comments or non-operational metadata lines per frozen equivalence rules, mark as semantically no-op.
Line-level mapping validation between verifier-labeled failure locations and the corresponding configuration AST node on a disjoint validation set.
automatic_rejection_rules: Automatically mark as harmful and count when a repair removes a line listed in the frozen 'protected-intent' schema (e.g., explicit protected ACL entries or mandatory interface states).
Automatically reject/flag any repair that causes simulator-detected reachability regressions relative to the faulty initial candidate.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Full automatic logging of all pre/post configs and tokenized diffs for every episode. A disjoint validation set (not in confirmatory 1..40) will be used to validate mapping and concordance before confirmatory execution; all logs hashed and archived.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Validate verifier label → config-line mapping on the disjoint concordance set. Concordance target: >= 90% exact-line mapping accuracy; if below target, report concordance shortfall and treat verifier-only results as exploratory in analysis.
residual_risks: Verifier-exploitation remains possible (LLM optimizing to pass verifier labels rather than true compliance); monitored via verifier↔simulator disagreement counts and harmful-change flags.
Semantic intent loss detection is rule-based and may miss subtle intent drift; residual undetected harmful edits are possible.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Per-fault-class power and vendor-feature diversity limitation: n=40 constrains inference at the fault-class level.
Verifier↔simulator concordance may not fully capture production device behavior despite disjoint validation; external-validity limits remain for production environments.
Possibility of model training-data overlap with public config templates (residual contamination risk despite detection procedures).
Harmful over-repair rule coverage is finite and may miss subtle semantic intent changes.
